facts.text: McConnellsville takes its name from Joseph McConnell, an early settler who arrived in 1814 and later served as the town’s first postmaster.
By the late 1800s, the hamlet boasted a chair factory employing about forty workers, canning operations, a wintergreen distillery, and a Methodist Episcopal church rebuilt in 1881.
McConnellsville lies along New York State Route 13, roughly five miles southeast of Camden, close to Fish Creek and the northern shore of Oneida Lake.
The Erie Canal’s side cut linked Fish Creek directly to the main canal at Higginsville, turning McConnellsville into a vital transportation hub in the early 19th century.
Early 1800s saw the construction of a sawmill in 1801, a gristmill around 1804, and Isaac Cook’s double‑log tavern, laying the economic foundation for the hamlet.
Fine sandy loam soils, such as the Honeoye series, dominate the area, providing deep, well‑drained ground that has made McConnellsville a productive farming community.
